children: The Trump administration is preparing to revise U.S. rules governing applications for new tobacco products, potentially making it easier and faster for products such as flavored vapes and nicotine pouches to win regulatory approval, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

The Food and Drug Administration could announce in the coming days that it will reconsider a 2021 rule setting out the scientific requirements for new tobacco applications, according to people familiar with the matter.

Possible changes include reducing some requirements for scientific studies and shortening review times, one of the people said. Newer products such as vapes and nicotine pouches currently do not qualify for a streamlined approval route available to older products such as cigarettes. Tobacco companies have criticized the FDA for taking years in some cases to review applications, despite a congressional mandate calling for decisions within about six months.

The administration says it wants to make products it views as potentially less harmful alternatives for adult smokers, including flavored vapes, more accessible while keeping nicotine away from children.

Public-health groups, however, argue that flavored products can attract young people and encourage first-time tobacco use. The potential changes follow a lawsuit filed earlier this month by manufacturers and retailers, including Altria's
NJOY, which accused the FDA of creating an “insurmountable logjam” for new product applications.
The move would mark a contrast with Trump's first term, when the FDA restricted fruit-flavored vapes to curb youth vaping.

title: U.S. weighs faster approval process for new vapes, nicotine pouches
